meaning.evidence: Every instruction survives, including the contrast between species: "keep your pack on and PLAY DEAD", "If you're attacked by a black bear, DO NOT PLAY DEAD", "Always leave the bear a way out." "back off slowly and sideways" slightly blurs "move away slowly and sideways", since backing off suggests moving backwards.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "not something to eat" for prey, "have a go at you" for attack, "Getting your tucker", "Clear out of the area". "back off slowly and sideways" strains a little against the sideways instruction.

authenticity.evidence: Natural plain Australian English: "Pick up small kids straight away.", "Help the bear work out that you're a human.", "stop a bear getting at your food".

register.evidence: A light level-2 touch, mostly plain rewording with "tucker", "have a go at you", "Clear out"; no swearing.

tone.evidence: Stays a calm, serious safety notice; capitals and warnings kept: "Do NOT run or make any sudden movements." "have a go at you" is casual but not flippant.

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "If the bear isn't moving, back off slowly and sideways; that way you can keep an eye on the bear and not trip over."

variety.evidence: Light slang, not repeated: "tucker" once, "have a go", "Clear out", "straight away".

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the NPS bear guidance, structure and emphasis intact through "do NOT play dead—fight back!"

problems.why: "back off" suggests moving backwards, slightly at odds with the sideways instruction in a safety text.

A.summary: A clean, natural light-touch version that keeps every safety instruction and the serious tone.

meaning.evidence: All instructions kept: "leave your pack on and PLAY DEAD", "DO NOT PLAY DEAD", "move away slowly and sideways". "groups also put bears off" softens "groups are also intimidating to bears" but keeps the point.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "tucker" for food, "pick up on groups of people from further away", "put bears off" for deterring them, "a way out".

authenticity.evidence: Natural and plain: "But do check the advice for each park you visit", "Pick up small kids straight away."

register.evidence: Level 2: a light rewording with "tucker" and "put bears off"; perhaps a shade lighter than A but on brief; no swearing.

tone.evidence: Serious and calm, warnings intact: "Do NOT climb a tree. Both grizzlies and black bears can climb trees."

flow.evidence: Smooth, with one echo: "Do NOT let the bear get at your tucker. Getting your tucker will only encourage the bear".

variety.evidence: Little slang, and "tucker" doubled in adjacent sentences.

essence.evidence: Clearly the NPS guidance, every section in order.

problems.quote: Do NOT let the bear get at your tucker. Getting your tucker
problems.original: Do NOT allow the bear access to your food. Getting your food

B.summary: A faithful, natural light-touch version; one repeated "tucker".

meaning.evidence: The original kept almost word for word, so instructions survive; "Pick up little fellas immediately" blurs "small children" in a safety line.

sense.evidence: "Pick up little fellas immediately" is a gendered pet term that in a bear notice could even read as small animals; "protecting tucker, cubs, or their space" puts a human-food word on the bear's own food. "Getting your tucker" fits.

authenticity.evidence: Slang dropped into formal US prose: "Pick up little fellas immediately." sits beside "Concentrate your kicks and blows on the bear's face and muzzle."

register.evidence: Lighter than level 2: almost entirely untranslated, e.g. "Once a bear has noticed you and is paying attention to you, additional strategies can help prevent the situation from escalating."

tone.evidence: The serious tone is the original's, though "Pick up little fellas immediately" introduces a cute note into an urgent instruction.

flow.evidence: Reads as the original with jolts at the swaps: "prevent a bear from accessing your tucker".

essence.evidence: It is the original, recognisable but barely retold.

problems.why: A pet term for boys in an urgent safety instruction; unclear and wrong register.

problems.quote: most bears are only interested in protecting tucker, cubs, or their space
problems.original: most bears are only interested in protecting food, cubs, or their space
problems.why: "tucker" applied to the bear's food strains.

problems.quote: additional strategies can help prevent the situation from escalating
problems.original: additional strategies can help prevent the situation from escalating
problems.why: Most of the text is left untranslated; under the level-2 brief.

C.summary: Essentially the original with "tucker" swaps and an ill-fitting "little fellas"; too light and occasionally odd.
